properties.description: The stopping rule for the tree cap:requirement-lineage now holds (Anthony, 2026-07-25). A requirement is ATOMIC when it cannot be split further without losing meaning and one person or team can build and test it. Without a termination condition a decomposition goes wrong in BOTH directions, and the second is the dangerous one because it looks like rigour: under-decomposed leaves a compound requirement nobody can test cleanly; OVER-decomposed turns requirements into task lists and code design (\"the system must lock the account after three failed attempts\" is atomic; \"the system must query the login_attempts column and check if the integer equals 3\" is not a requirement at all). THE SIGNALS SPLIT THE SAME WAY THE QUALITY CRITERIA DO (dec:three-party-checks), which is what makes this buildable rather than advice. CHEAP AND DETERMINISTIC — build first: NO CONJUNCTIONS, a literal scan of the statement for \"and\", \"or\", \"additionally\", which is a text check needing no model and catching the most common compound requirement; SINGLE OWNER, computable from the graph as whether the capabilities satisfying it allocate to ONE component, since a leaf whose delivery is spread across several parts is not one team's to own; SINGLE TESTING POINT, partly computable as whether it has exactly one check rather than several. SEMANTIC — the agent proposes, the human decides: ESTIMABLE, and OVER-DECOMPOSED, which is the same judgement as the minimally-constrained criterion in cap:requirement-quality seen from the other end — a requirement that dictates implementation and a requirement decomposed into implementation are the same error, and noticing that they are one thing means one detector can serve both. Pairs with cap:missing-sibling: that asks whether a family is missing a member, this asks whether its members are the right SIZE, and a family of uneven grain is a signal for both. PLANNED.
properties.name: Know when to stop decomposing — and when someone went too far

properties.description: From the same study: GitHub's server generates its instructions from the enabled toolsets and tells the agent in them to paginate in batches of 5-10 and pass minimal_output, and its result types carry field-selection enums whose comments name the heaviest fields. reflow2 has the same problem and lost to it twice in one session on 2026-07-25 — scan_nodes over 72 Decisions returned 96,000 characters and the harness had to spill it to a file before it could be read at all. The precedent for the shape is already in this design: BL-48/BL-49 gave propagate a bounded summary with the full dump behind full=true. This extends that to the readers that grew unbounded, with the rule that a cap is never silent: the page says how many nodes exist, how many came back, and how to get the rest.
properties.name: A read that would not fit answers with a bounded page and says what it left out

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as the brainstorm skill + the /brainstorm command. Anthony's brother's original ask ("work through planning and idea realization before committing concepts to graph... an agent-assisted thinking process"), reframed by Anthony into what it actually is: not a staging gate but a KIND of record. Ideas enter the graph immediately as `proposed` Decisions named as open questions, with the options in the decision text and the honest counter-argument beside each; nothing waits outside in a buffer where it could be forgotten, and nothing is claimed as intent. THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES IT WORK WAS ALREADY THERE, found while building: detect_gaps raises undecided_decision_point ONLY on a proposed Decision with two or more REGISTERED alternatives, so a Decision whose options live in prose is silent by construction — and the nudge to choose arrives exactly when register_alternative turns an option into a fork with a design behind it. The loop stays quiet while someone thinks, and speaks the moment the ideas stop being ideas. No label, no schema change, no upgrade doc. THE GUARDS, all prose because none is machine-checkable: never create Requirements or Capabilities from a brainstorm (promotion is a separate step needing the user's word); never argue an idea down in conversation — record the objection beside it, because an idea killed in dialogue loses its reasoning; never run detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes, which would ask the user to firm up exactly what they left soft; and never promote the last idea standing, since one remaining idea nobody chose is still an idea nobody chose. set_decision_status to `proposed` is mandatory, because add_decision defaults to `accepted` and would assert a settlement that never happened. Ends as a PROMOTION step, not a commit step: chosen ideas go through capture-intent, the rest stay recorded as considered rather than deleted (req:roads-not-taken). The one honest weakness is readability — a person scanning the decision list cannot tell a musing from a choice without reading the prose, which is what the open vocabulary question in dec:exploratory-staging is now reduced to.
properties.name: Work an idea through without committing to it, on the record

properties.description: Anthony's B+K / B-K case, 2026-07-25: the project does A, B, C and D, and the ask is to make B do something more (or less). Distinct from cap:onboarding (BL-101), which answers where a NEW thing belongs — this answers where an EXISTING thing gets extended or narrowed, and the difference matters because the answer is shaped by what B already touches rather than by where a gap is. Mostly composition of machinery that exists and has never been aimed at this question: search_design maps the user's words onto B; propagate_from gives the blast radius of touching it; the Decision layer says what already governs B and must not be casually contradicted; cap:requirement-lineage would say whether B is a decomposed child (so the parent's other children are siblings that may need the same change) or carries derived requirements that the extension might invalidate. THE SIMPLIFICATION DIRECTION IS THE INTERESTING HALF and is not symmetric with extension: removing capability from B means asking what still depends on it, which is propagate run the other way, and then whether any requirement is left unsatisfied by the removal — a question retire-from-design already forces for a whole node but nobody asks for a partial reduction. Removing is where designs are damaged quietly, because the thing that breaks is usually not the thing being edited. PLANNED.
properties.name: Show where to extend or simplify a feature that already exists

properties.description: Claim a region of the design so two people do not collide in it (BL-44). BUILT 2026-07-25 as claims.rs, exposed as claim_region / release_claim / claim_report (96 tools). A new CLAIMS edge, Contributor → any node, carrying depth / claimed_at / note. THE SHAPE IS SET BY dec:multi-writer-architecture, and every part of it follows from having no server. A CLAIM IS NOT A LOCK. Nothing in the module refuses a write and nothing anywhere consults a claim before allowing one; a second writer who ignores a claim gets a correct three-way merge exactly as if it did not exist. That is pinned by a test rather than promised in a comment, because a claims layer that READS like locking is worse than none — it invites reliance on a guarantee it cannot make. THE REGION IS COMPUTED, never stored: a claim holds a seed and a depth, and the membership is derived through the same traversal propagate_from uses, so it follows the design as the design changes instead of freezing a list that silently goes wrong the moment someone adds an edge (pinned: new work inside a claimed area is covered without re-claiming). OVERLAP IS REPORTED, NEVER PREVENTED. Two people may claim the same ground and both claims stand; claim_report names the shared nodes and ranks collisions by size, because a two-node brush and a forty-node collision should not read alike. Two claims by the SAME person are not a collision — reporting them would train people to ignore the list, which is how a signal dies. The advisory limit ships IN the payload, not only in the docs, since whoever reads it over the wire never sees the docs. CLAIMS is deliberately NOT a traceability edge, like AUTHORED_BY: who is working on something is coordination, not design structure, and propagating it would drag people into every blast radius (pinned by a test). 9 tests. Schema change: edge types 54 → 55.
properties.name: Claim a region of the design so two people do not collide in it

properties.description: Load N alternative design exports (branch-by-file) and report each branch on the same measures — graph_report snapshot (nodes, open gaps, allocation health, verification coverage) side by side — plus each branch's structural divergence from a named baseline (compare_designs). Alternatives comparable on measures, not advocacy. BL-70 v1; the collapse (merge winner + retire losers) reuses BL-80. Rung 2 wires the decision point.
properties.name: Compare parallel alternatives on the same measures (AoA)

properties.description: Diff two export documents (or the live graph against one) into added / removed / changed relative to a named base, banded into design content vs bookkeeping, property-level on changes.
properties.name: Compare two as-designed records

properties.description: Take a directory of written specifications and produce one coherent design from the whole corpus, keeping each claim's provenance Fragment pointing back at its source document. Extends single-document extraction, which already works, with the two things a corpus needs and a file does not: a folder driver, and identity resolution ACROSS documents so the same thing named in many specs converges on one node. The primitive for that convergence already exists — every node type declares its own resolution strategy and threshold in the schema — so this is wiring an existing mechanism at batch scale rather than inventing one. Bound by dec:ask-not-repair: suspected duplicates are asked, never silently merged, which at corpus scale means the asking must be batched or the feature is unusable. PLANNED — BL-97.
properties.name: Ingest a folder of specifications as one design

properties.description: Compare the design against an agent-supplied sweep of the real system and report the regions no node claims, ranked by mass, so the largest silences surface first. The sibling of reconcile_artifacts (design vs reality) and its opposite in subject: reconcile asks "has what I know about changed?", coverage asks "what is there that I have never been told about?". reflow2 performs no file I/O — the agent sweeps and supplies the paths, exactly as reconcile does with checksums. Measures CLAIMED REGIONS, never a file-count ratio, because the modelling doctrine mandates one artifact per meaningful unit and one opaque component for a vendored mass; counting files would punish correct coarse modelling. Excluded regions are named as excluded, never silently dropped. Reports the sweep's date so stale coverage is never read as current, and can record its result so a state-derived gap can be raised from it without detect_gaps needing arguments. PLANNED — BL-95.
properties.name: Say what the design has never heard of

properties.description: A proposed Decision is a decision point: register alternatives under it as lightweight Artifact pointers (branch-by-file, each naming its export), GOVERNED_BY the Decision and CONTRADICTS their siblings — the fork held open. Refuses registering under a settled decision. Collapse chooses a winner: the Decision moves to accepted, losers are superseded (OBSOLETES, retired on the record not deleted), and the outcome + rationale are written into the Decision's own alternatives field. The teeth: the undecided_decision_point DETECT gap surfaces a proposed Decision with >=2 alternatives as an open fork ('which do you choose?'), anchored so it clears on collapse. The winner's content-merge reuses apply_merge. BL-70 rung 2; ops set_decision_status, register_alternative, alternatives_for, collapse_decision.
properties.name: Hold and collapse a decision point (forkable alternatives)

properties.description: Derive a requirement's delivery state from the golden thread rather than reading a hand-set field. BUILT 2026-07-24 as `delivery_coverage()` in report.rs, surfaced on graph_report as `delivery` and as a line in the Markdown view. A requirement is DELIVERED when something satisfies it AND that capability is realized AND currently carries a passing check, at its own or component granularity. Two properties are load-bearing and both are pinned by tests. FIRST, it goes BACKWARDS: because capability_verification only reports Verified/ComponentVerified for checks that pass (dec:passing-is-verified), a requirement stops being delivered the moment its check starts failing, with nobody editing anything — a derivation that can only ratchet up is a stored claim with extra steps. SECOND, inference is not evidence: a requirement whose own provenance is `inferred` was read back out of the code implementing it, so its satisfaction is a tautology; those are counted apart as `inferred_only` rather than silently dropped, because otherwise a brownfield adopt would report itself fully delivered on arrival. Dropped requirements are excluded from the denominator — abandoning a need is not failing to deliver it. FIRST REAL ANSWER, against reflow2's own design the day it was built: 20 of 30 requirements delivered, 29 satisfied — a question that was flatly unanswerable an hour earlier, when zero requirements carried `met`. STILL TO DO from the original scope, deliberately not built here: distinguishing SUPERSEDED from DROPPED from EVOLVED, and surfacing MET-BUT-REGRESSED as a TemporalFact with VALID_TO. The headline number came first because it is what makes the rest legible.
properties.name: Compute what is delivered, and expose the requirement lifecycle that is currently unused

properties.description: Say which way the design and the build have diverged, not merely that they have. Anthony's founding problem, observed in the field 2026-07-24 (reflow2 on storyflow: the docs "consistently understate what's built") and the failure the predecessor died of. BUILT 2026-07-25, pieces 1 and 2 of 3. HOW: ObservedArtifact gains an optional `realizes` — what the caller observed the file actually implementing. Core compares that against the recorded REALIZES edges, which keeps the no-file-IO contract intact (the agent observes, the core computes) and yields both halves at once. DIRECTION: more observed than recorded is Understated, less is Overstated, each-having-what-the-other-lacks is Diverged. MEANING: the finding carries `unrecorded` and `unbuilt` — the specific design nodes involved — and the message names them, which is the answer to "what does the design now claim wrongly?" that a checksum could never give. Without it, accepting drift means asking someone to go find the delta themselves, and that is the labour that does not happen under load. FOUR JUDGEMENTS WORTH KNOWING. (a) Direction is assessed INDEPENDENTLY of the checksum: a design can be wrong from the day it was written, and tying this to checksum_change would miss the long-lived untouched files where understatement accumulates. (b) Overstatement outranks understatement and plain change, because a design claiming something absent is what someone will plan against — understatement is a record that is behind, overstatement is a record that is wrong. (c) `realizes: None` means not assessed and is never read as agreement, so no existing caller silently starts asserting alignment it never checked. (d) Mapped onto the EXISTING schema drift_types (understated records as undocumented_addition, which is what it is one level down; overstated as spec_mismatch) rather than adding two enum values — a schema change costs a minor bump, an upgrade doc and real pain for anyone on an older stamp (BL-94), and buys nothing here. NOT BUILT: piece 3, write-back to the source documents a design was adopted from. The graph can now be brought up to date; the markdown people actually read still cannot.
properties.name: Say which way the design and the build have diverged, and bring the design back up

properties.description: The plain-language entry surface: what reflow2 physically is, how it runs on the reader's own machine, where the agent instructions go, and a few concrete uses — before any doctrine. Realized by documentation artifacts (README, the getting-started material, diagrams) rather than by code, which is why it is a capability with no module: what satisfies it is prose and pictures. PLANNED — BL-102. Deliberately left unallocated at capture: which part of the project owns its own explanation is a real question, not an obvious one, and inventing an owner would be a renderer fill-in of the kind dec:views-are-projections forbids.
properties.name: Explain itself to someone who has not been convinced yet

properties.description: Keep every Decision's unchosen options as forkable siblings; re-open a past decision at its epoch and take a different branch, with the alternative's consequence design computed by replay (propagate/compare) rather than pre-stored. Selection of which fork to expand follows the reward signal — defects and field trials — not the whole tree; the human does the credit assignment. The navigation layer of reflow2-as-decision-MDP, unifying BL-70 (branches), BL-80 (merge, how a road comes home) and BL-44 (claims). DESIGNED 2026-07-24: the fork point is a coordinate, decision → AT_EPOCH → epoch.checksum → the committed export (dec:fork-point-address), so no ref/DAG layer is needed; re-opening mints a superseding Decision rather than un-accepting the original (dec:reopen-supersedes); the epoch chain the whole thing addresses is backfilled from real release tags (dec:temporal-backfill-from-releases). STILL TO BUILD: the read-only fork_point operation that resolves a Decision to its epoch, checksum and governed blast radius, and reports what has changed since — the base a three-way merge then takes to bring a road home.
properties.name: Hold and re-fork a decision's unchosen alternatives

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as `reflow2-mcp --merge-driver %O %A %B`, plus the `.gitattributes` entry and the parallel-work skill. THE PROBLEM IT ANSWERS, from Anthony's own doubt while brainstorming the isolation ideas: claiming a cluster of nodes says nothing about the REPOSITORY, so two people working entirely separate parts of one design still collide in git — the export is a single large JSON document and git merges it by lines, a unit that means nothing to a graph. The merge itself already existed (BL-80: per node, per property, against the common ancestor, conflicts minted as Questions with deterministic ids); what was missing was one adapter so git calls it. Git's contract followed exactly: exit 0 means merged with the result in %A, non-zero means conflicts remain and the path stays unmerged for a human. A clean merge is written and succeeds; a real both-sides conflict exits non-zero WITHOUT touching %A and prints each conflict id, its question and the `--merge-apply` command that finishes the job — because a driver that fails silently at a git prompt is how someone reaches for `--ours` and deletes a node the other person wrote. NOTHING IS AUTO-DECIDED: the driver applies only what one-sided changes make derivable, running the same resolve_merge the apply path uses so it can take no shortcut of its own. Tested by GIT, not by a home-grown client (tools/test_merge_driver.py, 4 cases on real branches): disjoint edits merge with no human, both-sides conflicts leave the path unmerged and name themselves, additions from both sides both survive, and an unconfigured clone degrades to git's text merge instead of failing — because .gitattributes travels with the repo and the driver definition cannot.
properties.name: Be git's merge driver for the design, so disjoint work merges itself

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25. `Interface.designation` (internal | published, defaulting to internal because publishing is a commitment nobody should have asserted for them) plus `set_interface_designation`, plus the computation that earns the distinction: `propagate_from` now reports `boundary_crossings` — the published Interfaces a change passes through, NAMED rather than counted, in both the full radius and the summary, with `crosses_published_boundary` on each impacted node. That makes severability computed instead of asserted, which is what MOSA's Table D-1 asks a program to demonstrate and what an architecture diagram cannot prove: a change inside a part either crosses none of the design's published boundaries, or the report says which contract carried it and therefore whom to talk to. WHY THE DISTINCTION WAS WORTH ADDING: two independent routes arrived at the same missing property — MOSA's designation of modular system interfaces (from the guidebook Anthony supplied) and BL-45's system-of-systems thread, which recorded five days earlier that nothing marks an Interface external-facing. dec:edge-orthogonality's rule is satisfied because a computation reads it. FOUND BY A TEST, and it was a real bug: the first implementation counted a boundary ONE HOP PAST the depth bound as crossed, so an internal change reported crossing a contract the walk never reached. The crossing bookkeeping now sits after the depth guard, where a boundary beyond the bound belongs to truncated_beyond_depth instead. Also pinned: seeding a change ON a published interface is not a crossing (you are changing the promise, not passing through it — conflating them would make every ICD edit look like a containment failure), and withdrawing a designation removes the crossing, because the computation follows the design rather than remembering it. 8 tests. NOT DONE, and named rather than implied: no filtered export of "just the published surface" (req:design-composes needs it), and no per-module modularity view — the acquisition community's words for these criteria belong in a projection, never in the schema.
properties.name: Designate a published boundary, and compute whether a change stays behind it

properties.description: Hold inviolable intent (KPPs) and COMPUTE when the design breaks one. BUILT 2026-07-25. Anthony's call on shape: a discriminated Constraint (`category: kpp`) rather than a new node type, because the quantity/limit/direction triple and the budget rollup are exactly what a KPP needs and already existed unused — and because an enum value plus a property is upgrade-SAFE where a new node type would refuse older binaries, which mattered on a day that already shipped two edge-type changes. Added `objective` beside the existing `limit`, giving the acquisition pair: threshold is the minimum acceptable, objective is what success looks like. Objective is optional and never invented, because a number the graph asserts on its own is the one thing intent vocabulary must not do. THREE VIOLATIONS, ranked ABOVE ordinary gaps because a breached KPP is not thinness in the design, it is the design failing. UNBOUND (0.90) — a KPP constraining nothing can never be violated, so it sits permanently green while asserting something vital; the quietest failure and the reason 'a KPP that nothing checks is a comment'. Reported once, not three times: an unbound KPP cannot also be breached or contradicted, and counting one fault three ways would teach people the findings are noise. BREACHED (0.95) — the budget rollup crossed the threshold, reusing budget_report wholesale. The only arithmetic violation, and the reason a KPP is worth distinguishing from a requirement nobody adds up. An INCOMPLETE rollup is deliberately NOT a breach: asserting failure from absent data is the silent guess this project forbids. CONTRADICTED (0.85) — an ACCEPTED decision governs what the KPP binds, surfaced for review and explicitly not asserted as a violation, since whether it truly costs the KPP is semantic. Proposed decisions are excluded: an open choice has traded nothing away, and flagging it would punish thinking out loud. 9 tests. FOUND WHILE BUILDING: GOVERNED_BY runs FROM the governed node TO the Decision, so the first implementation walked it backwards and found nothing — caught by the test rather than by review. THE CAPTURE HALF IS cap:kpp-proposal AND IS NOT BUILT: this computes violations of KPPs that exist; it does not notice that a stated need SHOULD be one.
properties.name: Hold inviolable intent (KPPs) and compute when the design breaks one

properties.description: The capture half of KPPs, and the half a person actually touches. BUILT 2026-07-25 as the kpp-proposal skill (art:kpp-proposal-skill) plus the typed write path it needs. Anthony, 2026-07-25: the user says "the system should be able to perform X"; the agent, acting as the systems-engineering SME the user is not required to be (req:no-se-knowledge), recognises the shape of inviolable intent and asks — that sounds like something that MUST be met, is it? — and the user confirms or declines. WHY THE AGENT MUST NOT DECIDE IT: criticality is a claim about consequence, not about wording. Whether missing a threshold FAILS THE EFFORT depends on mission, contract and money that the graph does not hold and the agent cannot see. An agent that promoted a requirement to KPP on its own would be asserting the user's stake in their own project, which is the same forgery dec:certainty-derived forbids for requirement status — and worse here, because a KPP outranks every ordinary gap and would drag the whole detector's ranking with it. So: the agent PROPOSES, the human DISPOSES, and nothing enters as a KPP without the user's word. WHAT THE AGENT CAN LEGITIMATELY NOTICE, and it is more than intuition. A statement carrying a unit-bearing threshold (500 miles, 3000 pounds, 500 milliseconds) is already shaped like a KPP and may simply be unmodelled — the quantity/limit/direction triple has somewhere to go. Language of necessity ('must', 'shall', 'no less than') against language of preference ('should', 'aims to') is a real signal in acquisition prose. And a requirement whose failure the user has elsewhere described as fatal is a candidate the graph itself can surface. THE QUESTION MUST CARRY THE CONSEQUENCE, not just the label: asking 'is this a KPP?' invites a shrug, whereas asking 'if the system missed this by ten percent, would the effort have failed?' is answerable by someone who has never heard the term — which is the test req:no-se-knowledge sets. FOUND WHILE BUILDING, and it was the reason this could not be skill-only: add_constraint had no `objective` parameter and its description never mentioned the kpp category, so the only way to record a confirmed KPP over MCP was the generic create_node — which is why the 9 tests of cap:kpp build their KPPs that way. A capture skill would have been pointing the agent at a door that was not there. add_constraint now takes objective and names the category, so what the user confirms is recordable through the typed helper (3 further tests). TWO GUARDS THE SKILL CARRIES that no test can enforce: it must not ask about every requirement (a design where everything is inviolable has no KPPs, and asking becomes noise the user waves through), and on a decline it records a small accepted Decision GOVERNED_BY the node, because the same signals will otherwise make it ask again next session — being asked the same question twice is how someone learns the tool is not listening. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT AUTOMATED: nothing scans the design for KPP candidates on its own. That would be a detector proposing the user's stakes to them, and the ask belongs where the words are still fresh — in the conversation that produced them.
properties.name: Notice when a stated need is really a KPP, and ask

properties.description: Given a common-ancestor export and two divergent records, compute a typed three-way merge per node and per property (git's trivial-merge case table over typed values, not lines): where only one side changed, take it; where both changed differently, surface a structured conflict as a Question rather than guessing. Deletion is retain-and-ask. The write-side sibling of cap:compare-designs. BL-80 #1+#2, the core of BL-12's merge. BUILT + VERIFIED (art:merge, ver:merge, 46 tests): merge_designs proposes (writes nothing); resolve_merge materialises the merged design from the human's per-conflict decisions; apply_merge commits it into the live graph atomically, refusing until every conflict is decided. Surfaces: merge_designs (read-only) + apply_merge (write) MCP tools; and the file-pure git-file pair of CLI modes --merge (propose, printing conflicts and their ids) and --merge-apply (apply a decisions file with resolve_merge, printing the merged export document, never touching the graph and refusing until every conflict is decided). Base is git's merge-base; the reflow2-native DAG is BL-70; rerere is BL-80 #5.

properties.description: Record how a human resolved a merge conflict — content-keyed (property + base/ours/theirs values, node-independent) — and offer it back when the same conflict recurs. Stored in the graph as an answered Question whose id IS the content key (rr: prefix; the Question schema has no source field, so the prefix distinguishes it and it stays invisible to open_questions). Advisory: recall_resolutions surfaces the recorded choice; the human confirms, or bulk-accepts via apply_merge use_recorded. BUILT + VERIFIED (art:merge, ver:merge): resolution_key on each property/edge-property conflict, record on apply, recall_resolutions tool. Extends cap:merge-designs; BL-80 #5. v1 covers property + edge-property conflicts (node-type/delete-modify keys deferred).
properties.name: Reuse a recorded conflict resolution (rerere)

properties.description: Anthony, 2026-07-25: "you have requirements A and C, but you missed B." A genuinely different kind of gap from everything detect_gaps finds today. Every existing gap source reasons about STRUCTURE — this requirement has no capability, this capability has no check — and each is deterministic because the hole is visible in the graph's shape. A missing requirement is invisible in the shape: the design is perfectly coherent without it, which is exactly why nobody notices. TWO AXES, and the user's fighter-jet example shows they are different detections. BREADTH is the bigger one: a stakeholder states that the wings must provide X lift and sustain Y G, and the engine must make Z thrust — two SUBSYSTEM-level requirements, which implies a subsystem decomposition in which landing gear, avionics, fuel, flight controls, life support, structures, hydraulics and thermal have nothing whatsoever. That is not interpolating a missing item between two others; it is noticing that 2 of roughly 12 expected subsystems have been named at all, which requires knowing what kind of thing is being built. DEPTH is the second: the wing requirement is itself thin, since wings need more than lift and G-load. Both are semantic — pattern-matching against a domain archetype — so they belong to the LLM half of dec:three-party-checks, not the deterministic core. Bounded accordingly: the agent proposes, the graph records at `proposed`, the human decides, and nothing enters above proposed, or the tool starts inventing intent and dec:human-decides is broken in the way that matters most. cap:requirement-lineage sharpens it considerably — requirement families (which Leiden already clusters, once requirement-to-requirement edges exist) are precisely where an omission is both most likely and most detectable, because a family with two members in a design whose siblings have twenty is visible without knowing any domain at all. PLANNED.
properties.name: Notice the requirement nobody wrote down

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as `export_surface`. The first piece of req:design-composes, and deliberately the piece that EVERY answer to dec:nested-graphs needs: whatever composes, it composes through a published boundary rather than by reaching into another system's internals. Also the openness half of req:key-interfaces ("a design that publishes a surface should be able to export exactly that surface"). Contents: every Interface designated `published`, the artifacts that SPECIFIES or REALIZES it, the Components on each side, and the Project so a recipient knows whose surface they hold. Requirements, capabilities, decisions, verifications, history and every internal component stay home. Nodes are exported AS STORED — nothing trimmed or rewritten, because a fabricated node would import as a lie; what leaks internals is the graph BENEATH a component, and that is what is excluded. THE HONEST HALF, and the reason this is not just a filter: a recipient cannot tell a small design from a heavily filtered one, so the result counts and NAMES what it withheld, and says what the document is not ("not a backup"). A design with no designated boundary gets an EMPTY SURFACE warning rather than a quietly empty file — that case is dangerous precisely because it is indistinguishable from having nothing to share, and someone could publish it believing otherwise. It is NOT refused, because "prove I publish nothing" is a legitimate question. FOUND BY IMPACT-CHECK, before writing any code: propagate_change on cap:portability put dec:export-hash-chain in the direct ring, which is what stopped the surface from joining the file's hash chain. A derived view that advanced prev_content_hash would make compare_designs treat a published surface as an ancestor of the full design. FOUND BY A TEST: link_artifact writes REALIZES while the schema's intent for a contract artifact is SPECIFIES, so an ICD registered the ordinary way was missing from the surface. Both edges are honoured now — one is the contract as written, the other as built, and a recipient needs whichever exists. 7 tests, including the round trip: the other side imports it with zero skipped edges, gets the contract, and does not get our requirements.
properties.name: Publish just the boundary — the contracts others may rely on, and nothing internal

properties.description: Read requirements, functions and features back out of tests and their results, for the case where that is most or all of what survives — no specification, thin documentation, sometimes not even readable source, but a suite that says what the system was expected to do and a result set saying whether it did. Alex's observation, 2026-07-24. An expansion of cap:adopt rather than a rival: adopt already names tests among its evidence sources and already registers each suite as a Verification on the component it covers. What is new is the degenerate case, where tests are the PRIMARY source, so adopt's ordinary method does not apply — 'structure from imports and calls, never from prose' assumes a repo to read, and there may not be one. THE LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT, and the reason this needs its own computation rather than a paragraph in the adopt skill: a requirement recovered from a PASSING test is verified by construction. The test that produced the requirement is the same test that would prove it, so the golden thread closes on itself and the recovered design reads as fully delivered the moment it is created, having demonstrated nothing. This is the schema's `inferred` provenance trap one turn sharper — with code you get satisfied-by-construction, with test results you get satisfied AND verified by construction, which would defeat cap:derived-completion (BL-104) outright. So: intent recovered from a test must be marked as such, and must NOT count that same test as its verification evidence. A test-derived requirement is a claim about what someone once intended, not proof that it holds today. Corollary worth keeping: a FAILING test is the more informative artifact of the two, because it states an intent the system does not currently meet — which is a genuine gap, and the one thing in this whole area that cannot be circular. PLANNED.
properties.name: Recover intent from test evidence, without letting the tests prove themselves

properties.description: Hold the requirement tree. BUILT 2026-07-25. A new DECOMPOSES edge (Requirement → Requirement, child→parent, a traceability edge so requirement families cluster on their own meaning) plus a `lineage` property (original / decomposed / derived). Before this reflow2 had ZERO requirement-to-requirement edges: a systems-engineering tool holding requirements as a flat list. THE COMPUTATION THAT EARNS IT, and the half that is built: DELIVERY NOW ROLLS UP. cap:derived-completion credits a decomposed parent through its children instead of demanding it carry a capability of its own — EVERY child, not any, because a parent half-delivered is not delivered and `any` would let one finished slice of a checkout system report the whole thing done. The roll-up inherits the property that made delivery a derivation rather than an assertion: it goes backwards, so a child's check starting to fail un-delivers the parent with nobody editing anything. `decomposes` refuses a cycle, because a tree containing itself has no leaves and could never roll up honestly; it also sets the child's lineage, so the edge and the label cannot disagree — letting them would make the classification a second thing to maintain, which is how the requirement lifecycle went unused in the first place. Exposed over MCP as `decomposes` and `set_requirement_lineage` (93 tools), because a capability with no door is the failure this project found in `ingest` earlier the same week. SCHEMA CHANGE: edge types 53 → 54, so a graph written by this build is refused by older binaries with 'update reflow2' — the additive direction, which is loud and correct, and the one BL-86's set-based stamp made unambiguous. STILL TO BUILD: the derived half's teeth — naming, when a Decision is re-opened, the requirements that existed only because of the road taken. The vocabulary and the link are in place (lineage `derived` + GOVERNED_BY the Decision); the query is not.
properties.name: Hold the requirement tree: original, decomposed, derived

properties.description: The INCOSE-style criteria Anthony brought from acquisitions, 2026-07-25: a good requirement is unambiguous, verifiable, necessary, minimally constrained (implementation-free), traceable, feasible and consistent. THE USEFUL STRUCTURE IS THAT THEY DO NOT ALL BELONG TO THE SAME PARTY (dec:three-party-checks). THREE ARE STRUCTURAL and the core can judge them deterministically today or nearly so. TRACEABLE is already half-built — unsatisfied_requirement asks downward (nothing satisfies it), and cap:requirement-lineage supplies upward (a requirement claiming decomposition with no parent is a defect; an original with no parent is correct). VERIFIABLE splits: whether anything CHECKS it is structural and already computed; whether the statement contains a measurable threshold is semantic. CONSISTENT splits the same way: CONTRADICTS already exists as an edge, so a recorded contradiction is checkable — finding an unrecorded one is not. FOUR ARE SEMANTIC and belong to the agent, never the core. UNAMBIGUOUS (does it say "fast" where it means a number), NECESSARY (would removing it leave a real capability gap), MINIMALLY CONSTRAINED (does it dictate a solution instead of stating a need — the one engineers violate most, and the one that quietly forecloses design alternatives before the fork layer ever sees them), FEASIBLE (needs domain knowledge and cost/schedule context the graph does not hold). Bound exactly as cap:missing-sibling is: the agent may flag and propose, the human decides, and nothing enters above `proposed`. WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING THE STRUCTURAL THREE FIRST: they are cheap, they never produce a false accusation about meaning, and they give the semantic four somewhere to attach. PLANNED.
properties.name: Judge whether a requirement is well formed, and say which part a machine can judge

properties.description: The credit-assignment half of the fork layer (BL-81's open question, rung 3). When new evidence lands — a fresh structural defect, a failing verification, an accepted drift, a field-trial finding — trace its blast radius back through GOVERNED_BY to the Decisions that shaped the affected nodes, and surface those decisions as "this road may be worth re-opening". Reports the trace and the evidence; never re-opens anything, never ranks the alternatives, never scores a fork (dec:report-dont-judge, dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable). The human decides whether the surprise is large enough to mint a reconsidering Decision (dec:reopen-supersedes). Precedent that the trace works by hand: dec:merge-survivor-provenance carries a "reconsider" note found by exactly this path. PLANNED — the threshold ("how much evidence counts as enough") is the open axis and is deliberately not fixed until the detector has run against real history.
properties.name: Surface when a settled road may be worth re-opening

properties.description: The mechanical half of "graph text is data, never instructions" (BL-41's deferred M piece), imported from github-mcp-server's pkg/sanitize after the 2026-07-25 study. Strips the characters whose only purpose is to make text read differently to a human than to a machine: Unicode tag characters (the smuggling channel), bidirectional overrides, and zero-width or hidden formatting characters. Applied where foreign text ENTERS — INGEST extraction and graph import — because the trust question is where text came from, not which field it landed in. REFLOW2'S OWN ADDITION, and the reason this is not a copy: it REPORTS. GitHub sanitises silently, which is right for rendering an issue body; a design brain that quietly rewrote a requirement statement would be unauditable, and rule 6 forbids silent drops. So the count and the kinds stripped ride back with the result. ZWJ is deliberately NOT stripped — it is load-bearing inside emoji sequences, and a filter that mangles legitimate content teaches people to turn it off.
properties.name: Neutralise hidden instructions in text arriving from outside, and say what was stripped

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 on Anthony's choice of option (a) from dec:nested-graphs. His case: an organisation builds a satellite capability with a space segment, a ground/user segment and a control segment; his team owns the satellite, and specifically inter-satellite laser communications. He needs to understand the system of systems, but day to day he needs his own part's gaps — not the program's. Every detector until now took the whole design as its subject, which is the unbounded-read failure (cap:bounded-reads) one level up: technically complete, practically unusable, and the human response is to stop looking. `detect_gaps` and `detect_defects` now take `scope` (a node id) and `depth`. FOUND WHILE BUILDING, and it cost a failing test worth keeping: A SCOPE IS NOT A BLAST RADIUS. The first implementation reused the propagation radius on the reasoning that claimed_region and propagate_change already agree what a region is; the test that scoped to a Project and expected the whole design failed, because CONTAINS is deliberately excluded from the traceability rules (propagating along it would make the Project a hub short-circuiting every sibling to two hops). That exclusion is right for IMPACT — a change to a segment does not implicate every screw inside it — and wrong for OWNERSHIP, where a segment lead owns what is inside their segment by definition. So a scope is containment closure (unbounded: ownership does not attenuate with distance) then traceability radius (bounded: the thread reaches into other people's work and must stop). A CONSEQUENCE RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENTLY FIXED: claim_region still uses the radius alone, so claiming a segment does not claim the subsystems inside it — possibly a defect in the claims layer, but changing what a claim covers changes what two people believe they hold, so it is Anthony's call. SECOND FINDING, also from a test: the first filter silently dropped gaps that anchor on nothing — the lifecycle-phase gaps, which are statements about the design as a whole. That was the exact silent-drop this feature exists to prevent, so findings now land in exactly one of four buckets that sum to the total: in_scope, out_of_scope, unanchored, and project_level counted within in_scope. A scoped answer can therefore never imply the rest of the program is clean, and filtering never becomes the tool deciding what a team is allowed to worry about — a project-level rollup still reaches a team when it touches their work, carrying its own scope so they can see whose finding it is. NOT DONE: graph_report is a rollup, not a detector, and scoping it means per-subtree delivery denominators and modularity — a different job, deliberately not smuggled in here.

properties.description: Session takeaways as first-class graph content: each key decision, finding or realization written when it happens, anchored to the epoch of the session that produced it, and queryable afterwards by the agent as its own prior context. THE FRAMING THE USER SETTLED 2026-07-25, which moves this out of 'agent convenience' entirely: a session's context IS documentation — the how-and-why record of a design's evolution — and documentation is part of the product (sys:documentation, his fighter-jet argument). So this is not memory for the agent's benefit; it is internally-derived design documentation, produced by the work rather than written about it afterwards. That reframing matters because it changes the standard: a convenience can be skipped under load, a deliverable cannot. Decision.rationale and ChangeEvent already capture fragments of the why; what lives only in the session is the connective tissue — what was tried, what was rejected and on what grounds, which findings turned up while doing something else. The substrate landed with the fork layer: an epoch is a session-addressable point, decisions anchor to epochs, change events pin there. The trigger is the load-bearing gap: the existing handoff enforcement watches the modification time of MARKDOWN files, so the only mechanism forcing a session to leave takeaways behind points AWAY from the graph. Reflow2's own doctrine already states the principle in the authored_by contract — record it when a decision is made, not at session end. THE TRANSCRIPT POINTER: each session has a full local record at ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl, modelled as a Fragment, with nodes distilled from the session YIELDED from it. Two constraints. The session UUID is the portable identity and the absolute path only a machine-scoped hint, because a path stored as identity resolves for one person on one machine and silently misses for everyone on a shared graph. And a pointer to a 3 MB transcript is a RECEIPT, not documentation: leaning on it recreates the markdown problem one level down, since 'it is all in the transcript' is the same excuse as 'it is all in the backlog file'. PLANNED.
properties.name: Record and query what a session learned

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as the `find_tools` tool. Imported from github-mcp-server's pkg/tooldiscovery, which fuzzy-searches its own tool list with weighted scoring and returns three results by default. reflow2 serves 97 tools, and req:agent-native's promise — every capability reachable from a coding agent over one surface — is only true in principle if the agent can find the tool: a surface too large to hold in context is reachable the way a library with no catalogue is readable. Scored over `tool_router.list_all()`, the served surface itself, so the catalogue cannot drift from the tools that exist — the failure mode skill_lint exists to catch in prose, avoided here by construction rather than by a second list. Weights follow the source: an exact name outranks a name substring, which outranks a description hit, which outranks a parameter-name hit. Ties break by name so the same query answers the same way twice, because a ranking that reshuffles teaches an agent not to trust it. Summaries come back trimmed to the first sentence — a catalogue that costs as much to read as the surface it indexes is pointless — and the result names `matched`, `omitted` and `searched`, so a query that found nothing says so instead of falling back to the whole list.

properties.description: The answer to "what is the most pressing item?" once the backlog lives in the graph. It is NOT detect_gaps and NOT check-health, and the distinction is the design: detect_gaps asks what the design has not yet decided, check-health asks what shape is wrong, and this asks which of the agreed things to do now. Three different questions needing three different actions, often from three different people. Composed rather than invented — BL-85 already specifies the form ("a backlog_report / roadmap projection, a view, never a second source of truth"), BL-68 supplies readiness and risk-to-completion ("the roadmap is a risk-burndown schedule"), BL-40 is the projection layer, and the long narratives stay as documents-linked artifacts rather than being crushed into properties. THE RANKING RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: an unmade decision outranks the work waiting on it. A proposed Decision with things GOVERNED_BY it is a blocker, and pointing someone at blocked work is worse than saying nothing, because it looks like progress. Measured 2026-07-24, this is not hypothetical: dec:multi-writer-architecture blocks two nodes, so the honest answer to "what is next" right now is a decision only the human can make, not a build task. PREREQUISITE, and the reason this cannot usefully ship first: today ZERO accepted requirements lack a satisfying capability, so "what is unbuilt" is unanswerable from the graph — everything accepted is allocated to something. Distinguishing allocated from delivered needs cap:derived-completion (BL-104). Until that lands, this view can rank what is undecided and what is misshapen but is blind to what is merely unfinished. PLANNED.
properties.name: Say what to work on next, as a projection with its reasoning shown

properties.purpose: The fork module: analysis of alternatives across branch exports, the decision point (a proposed Decision holding forkable siblings), its collapse into a winner plus retired losers, and — planned — the fork point that resolves a past Decision to the design it was made against.

properties.name: claims
properties.purpose: The coordination module: who has which region of the design in hand, and where two people are working the same ground. Advisory only — it holds no locks and refuses no writes, because the design lives as a file in each checkout with no shared server to hold one (dec:multi-writer-architecture). Regions are computed from a seed and a depth via the same traversal propagate_from uses, so they follow the design rather than freezing a membership list.

properties.name: docs

properties.name: merge

properties.name: sanitize

properties.decision:
EPIGRAPH — "Two roads diverged in a wood, and I— / I took the one less traveled by, / And that has made all the difference." — Robert Frost, 'The Road Not Taken'. Aptly, the poem is itself a hindsight tale: the speaker concedes the two roads were worn 'really about the same' and foresees telling it 'with a sigh' ages hence — the difference is authored in retrospect, not known at the fork. That is this decision's whole bet: credit for a road taken is assigned in hindsight, by the human, never scored in advance. (Unofficially, 'the Robert Frost decision.')

reflow2 holds every Decision's alternatives as UNRANKED, forkable siblings — not a scored trade-study runner-up. The design is modelled as a navigable decision-MDP: the graph is the world-model (propagate/detect/compare evaluate a fork's consequences before anything is built), branches are the replay, and the reward signal is two-channel — the structural detectors (in-model holes: SPOFs, cycles, gaps) plus field trials (out-of-model holes only a real episode reveals, e.g. BL-74's loop-on-virtue collapse). Alternatives are stored cheaply (the unchosen option + its rationale, at the decision's epoch) and their consequence design is COMPUTED on demand by forking that epoch and replaying — never eagerly maintained as N full parallel designs, which would combinatorially explode and rot as the main line moves on (a non-stationary design). Which fork to expand is chosen by where the surprise is — a fresh defect, a failed trial, or a rationale that already flags doubt points back to a decision (high 'TD error') — not by enumerating the whole tree. Crucially the human is the reward function and does the credit assignment and policy update; reflow2 supplies the replay buffer and the world-model but never auto-optimizes a design by replay-and-score.
properties.name: Alternatives are unranked forkable siblings; the human judges in hindsight, not a stored score
properties.rationale: User decided the ranked-vs-unranked scope 2026-07-22 after developing the idea across three framings — choose-your-own-adventure (the decision tree you can turn back to), Analysis of Alternatives (the runner-up kept live), and a reinforcement-learning gridworld (replay an episode until you cross without falling in a hole). Unranked over a scored AoA because reflow2 routes judgment to the human (dec:report-dont-judge, dec:three-party-checks): a stored ranking would be the system asserting a preference it cannot honestly hold, and design episodes are too few, too expensive and too subjective for a stationary reward anyway. Derived-over-stored (store the fork, compute the consequence) is reflow2's recurring lesson (dec:certainty-derived, dec:component-verified-computed) and the only defence against an eagerly-maintained alternative rotting under a moving main line. Model-based-planning-not-model-free-crashing is the whole point of a design brain: propagate_change computes the blast radius before you edit, so you simulate the hole instead of falling in it — but BL-74 proves some holes are out-of-model and only a field episode finds them. This unifies the branch (BL-70), merge (dec:merge-three-way / dec:merge-conflict-semantics — how a forked road comes home) and claims (BL-44) threads under one primitive: alternatives as first-class, forkable, comparable, mergeable. The hindsight pass that motivated it is the mechanism already working by hand — dec:merge-survivor-provenance carries a 'reconsider' note tracing a near-bad merge back to its own fork. Deferred to their own decisions: how an alternative attaches to a Decision in the schema, the fork/branch ref layer (BL-70), the 'when has an episode taught us enough to revise' trigger, and the tool surface.

properties.rationale: A named gap says something is wrong NOW; a nudge says what comes next. Ranking 'next' above 'broken' made three brownfield trials do the useless thing first. Nudges are demoted, never suppressed. Decided 2026-07-19 (https://claude.ai/code/session_013aumVdHrRHu24cLirn6Cam); evidence: gap-surfacing disciplines 3 and 8.

properties.rationale: apply_heal deletes a node with no undo, so merge is safe only because the endpoints were asserted; a heuristic must not drive it. A gap can be acknowledged, a HEAL defect cannot be dismissed. Decided 2026-07-19 (https://claude.ai/code/session_013aumVdHrRHu24cLirn6Cam); evidence: 3dtictactoe trial, BL-27/BL-29.
