A system that already exists can be brought under design control
properties.statement: Requirements, functions and structure can be recovered from a running system.

properties.name: An agent can drive the whole loop
properties.statement: Every capability is reachable from a coding agent over one surface.

properties.name: Any level of the design can be analysed on its own, and a narrowed answer says what it left out
properties.statement: A person or team responsible for one part of a design must be able to point the detectors at that part and be answered about it — "is my subsystem coherent, what is it owed" — without reading the whole program. Anthony, 2026-07-25, from the satellite case: an organisation building a satellite capability has a space segment, a ground/user segment and a control segment; his team owns the satellite, and more specifically inter-satellite laser communications. He must understand the system of systems, but day to day he needs his own part. Two properties are inseparable from the first. A narrowed answer must NAME WHAT IT WITHHELD — findings elsewhere in the design, and findings that belong to no part in particular — because a team shown only its own corner will conclude the program is healthy, which is the silent-drop failure req:no-silent-fallback forbids, one level up from a truncated read. And narrowing must never become the tool deciding what a team is allowed to worry about: a program-level finding that touches their work still reaches them, marked as the program's rather than theirs. Deliberately silent on WHERE the levels live: a subtree of one graph and a design of its own are both answers to this, and that is the architecture question recorded as dec:nested-graphs.

properties.name: As-designed vs as-built divergence is detectable
properties.statement: Real files on disk are registered as checksummed Artifacts realizing capabilities, so drift between the design and the build is visible rather than assumed.

properties.name: Design stays coherent across its lifecycle
properties.statement: When anything changes in any phase, the ripples are found and surfaced.

properties.name: Whether intent has been delivered is computed from the golden thread, never asserted
properties.statement: A requirement's completion must be derived from evidence already in the graph — something satisfies it, and that capability is realized and its check passes — not set by hand on the requirement itself. A hand-set "done" is a claim that outlives the truth: it survives the capability regressing, the artifact drifting, the verification starting to fail, and it degrades exactly as silently as an unreconciled checksum. Derived completion also makes the reverse question answerable without anyone maintaining it: what fraction of accepted intent is actually delivered, and which requirements are believed-done on evidence that no longer holds. The same rule applies to the rest of the lifecycle: a requirement that stopped being satisfied must be able to say so, rather than remaining green because nobody revisited it.

properties.name: Several people can plan against one design without colliding
properties.statement: A team, not a single author, must be able to work on one design at the same time: each person able to see what the others hold, to work in a scope that does not collide with theirs, and to have genuinely overlapping work surfaced as decidable conflicts rather than silent last-writer-wins. Whether this extends to simultaneous editing with live presence, or stops at non-colliding parallel work with good merges, is deliberately not asserted here — it depends on an architecture question that is still open, and the weaker form may be what teams actually need.

properties.name: A whole corpus of existing specifications can be brought into the design in one pass
properties.statement: Where a system's intent already exists as a large body of written specifications, reflow2 must be able to take the whole corpus — a folder, not a file — and produce one coherent design from it, with every claim still pointing back at the document it came from. The load-bearing requirement is identity ACROSS documents: the same component named in forty specifications must converge on one node rather than forty near-duplicates, and where convergence is uncertain the user is asked rather than the nodes being silently merged. Ordering must not decide meaning — which file happened to be read first must not determine the canonical name of anything.

properties.name: The design must be able to say how much of the system it has never modelled
properties.statement: reflow2 must be able to report the portion of a real system that no node in the design has ever claimed, so that the thinness of a recovered or evolving model is measurable rather than merely felt. An empty gap list must mean "the design is coherent AND it covers the system", not "the design is coherent about the fraction it happens to know". The report says what is unclaimed and how large it is; it never scores the design, never blocks, and never treats coarse-but-honest modelling as a deficiency — a single opaque Component legitimately claims everything beneath it.

properties.name: Recording an open question must never assert that it was settled
properties.statement: A Decision's status must not be set on the user's behalf. Recording a choice someone is still facing — an open question, a brainstormed option, a decision point held for later — must land as `proposed`, and reaching `accepted` must be a separate, deliberate act. Found as friction 2026-07-25: add_decision defaults to `accepted`, so six open questions recorded in one session each landed as settled and needed correcting immediately afterwards. This generalises dec:certainty-derived from requirements to decisions, and the reason is the same: an accepted Decision is what where-am-i reads back to the user as "what you decided", what the fork layer treats as binding, and what the KPP contradiction check reads as a trade already made. A musing recorded as a reasoned choice is therefore worse than a missing record — it is a false one, attributed to them. Evidence it was systemic rather than one slip: the correction had become a standing note carried across sessions, and the brainstorm skill had to instruct it in prose ("this call is not optional"), which is a defect with a bandage on it.

properties.name: Design anything, not only software
properties.statement: Software, hardware, a document, a process — the vocabulary stays neutral.

properties.name: A system's design can be a unit of its own that composes with the designs around it
properties.statement: Anthony, 2026-07-25, promoting the idea he had been thinking out loud about: "being able to have multiple repos that are linked by interface specifications (reflow2 could take both graphs and figure out how to resolve differences between those two repos to ensure they work together)... the idea would allow teams to focus in their most immediate concern and let the interface take care of how it works with all the other systems/components." The intent is that a design need not be one document for one program: a team owning a system can hold ITS design as a unit — its own store, its own lifecycle, its own published surface — and that unit composes with the systems around it through the interfaces between them, so the day-to-day view is genuinely local and the cross-system agreement is carried by the contract rather than by everyone reading everything. Four things follow, each a real obligation rather than a detail. The link between two designs cannot be an edge, because the schema validates both endpoints of every edge and they live in different stores; it must be a COORDINATE that names the other design, the node in it, and the version of it being built against. A parent's view of a composed child must ROLL UP the child's evidence — what it delivers and what it has proven — or a requirement satisfied inside the child fires as unsatisfied in the parent forever. That view is a dated claim about a VERSION of the child, never a live truth, so staleness is part of the model and not an afterthought. And the seam becomes the place where two teams genuinely collide, which is precisely where the merge machinery does not yet reach. This restates in the design what BL-45 recorded on 2026-07-20 from the same author, and it is deliberately silent on federation-versus-one-graph, which is dec:nested-graphs.

properties.name: Someone without the repo can reach a design, read it, and contribute to it
properties.statement: Anthony and his brother work on each other's ideas from opposite coasts, and today the only way to reach a design is to clone the repository that carries it. The intent is that a design can be made reachable to a named collaborator without handing them the code: they can read what it says, ask it questions, and contribute intent back — the collaboration is on the DESIGN, which is often the part a second person can help with before they know anything about the implementation. Two things this must not become. It must not make the design's home ambiguous: whatever hosts a shared copy, the repo file stays the durable record, or a hosting outage becomes a design outage (req:persistence, dec:repo-file-embedded). And it must not silently widen who can write: reaching a design is not the same as authoring in it, so a contribution must be attributable to a person (the Contributor layer, which exists) and the reach must be granted rather than assumed. Whether this is served by git remotes that already span both coasts, by a hosted service, or by both, is the open question recorded as dec:central-host — this requirement states the need, not the machinery.

properties.name: The core is deterministic and LLM-free
properties.statement: The runtime core must be free of LLM and provider dependencies and neutral to the interaction surface; LLM reasoning enters only behind a sync, object-safe seam.

properties.name: Drift is reported with its direction and its meaning, not just its magnitude
properties.statement: When the design and the build diverge, reflow2 must say which way and about what — not merely that a file's contents moved. Three things follow. Direction: a system that has grown capability the design never recorded is a different condition from one whose design overstates it, and today both arrive as an identical checksum change, so understatement is invisible exactly where it is largest. Meaning: the report must say what the design now claims wrongly, because asking someone to decide whether the design still holds while telling them only that bytes changed puts the entire burden of finding the delta on the person least likely to have time for it — which is how the design goes stale despite a mechanism designed to stop it. And write-back: where the design was recovered from documents, bringing the design up to date must be able to reach those documents, or the source everyone actually reads stays wrong while the graph quietly becomes right.

properties.name: The driving agents are coding agents, not humans
properties.statement: The primary consumers are Claude Code and grok build (plus OpenCode/Copilot), which reach the system as MCP tools plus an installed skill kit. The human is reached only through the agent.

properties.name: reflow2 explains what it is and how to run it before it explains what it believes
properties.statement: Someone arriving at reflow2 cold must learn, in plain language and before any philosophy, what it physically is and how it runs on their machine: a binary they run locally, a design graph kept as a file in their own repository, and a coding agent that talks to it over MCP. They must then find where the agent instructions go and two or three concrete uses — starting a design from nothing, recovering one from a system that already exists, and asking what breaks if something changes. The doctrine that makes reflow2 worth using is not the entry point to it.

properties.name: Install is one command, update is one word
properties.statement: A consumer installs reflow2 with a single command from a stable public URL (curl | bash or the platform equivalent) and updates with a single short command; releases are frequent and very minor, so updating is routine and cheap rather than an event. Modeled on the Claude Code installer/update experience the user named as the target (2026-07-20).

properties.name: Every artifact traces to the intent it serves
properties.statement: Traceability runs from concept through operations without a break.

properties.name: Gaps become questions, not guesses
properties.statement: Where the design is underspecified, the system must ask the human in plain language and record the answer, rather than silently choosing a default.

properties.name: The past is never overwritten
properties.statement: Updating the design to match the build must not erase what was intended.

properties.name: Intent that must hold no matter what is recorded as inviolable, and a violation is computed, not remembered
properties.statement: A design must be able to record intent that no downstream decision may trade away — a key performance parameter, in the acquisition sense: a threshold that, if missed, fails the effort regardless of how well everything else went. Inviolable intent is distinct from a Requirement (a goal to achieve, tradeable against other goals) and from a Constraint (a limit imposed on the design). reflow2 must (a) let that intent be stated with its threshold and, where it applies, its objective value; (b) COMPUTE a violation rather than rely on anyone remembering — an accepted Decision, an allocation, or a change whose blast radius contradicts a KPP must be surfaced loudly and above ordinary gaps; and (c) show a KPP crossing in impact analysis BEFORE the edit is made, not after it has been committed. A KPP that nothing checks is a comment.

properties.name: Invoked as an MCP server over stdio
properties.statement: The user-facing surface is the reflow2-mcp binary spoken to over stdio, installed into a consumer project by tools/reflow2_init.py, which merges rather than overwrites existing agent configuration.

properties.name: The design says which interfaces are the published boundaries, and computations read that distinction
properties.statement: Some interfaces are the boundary a system is known by; most are internal plumbing. The design must be able to say which — and the distinction must earn its keep by being read, not merely stored (dec:edge-orthogonality). From the MOSA guidebook Anthony supplied (OUSD(R&E), February 2025), whose entire discipline turns on designating modular system interfaces and then holding them stable and open, and independently from BL-45's system-of-systems thread, which found the same hole from the other side: nothing marks an Interface external-facing, so "visible to others" versus "mine to change" is undeclarable. Two independent routes to one missing property. What must read it, or the designation is decoration: a change that crosses a published boundary is a different risk from one that stays behind it, and impact analysis should say which it is BEFORE the edit; a design that publishes a surface should be able to export exactly that surface and nothing internal; and a composed design (req:design-composes) links through published boundaries, never through another system's internals. What this must NOT become: an assertion that a boundary is stable. Whether a published interface has in fact held is a matter of evidence — its drift history — not a property anyone sets.

properties.name: One reflow2 can hold several designs, and a session says which one it is working on
properties.statement: A person works on more than one project at a time, so reflow2 must be able to hold more than one design without their contents mixing, and a session must state which design it is operating on before it can read or write. Anthony, 2026-07-25: he has reflow2 itself and storyflow; his brother has several. Three properties follow. Selection is EXPLICIT — a session that has not named its design must be refused rather than defaulted to the last one used or the only one present, because a tool call landing in the wrong project is a silent corruption that no gap detector would ever notice. Segregation is enforced by the store, not by convention: every node and edge already carries a graph_id, which is exactly the primitive this needs, and today it is pinned to the constant "reflow2" — so the mechanism exists and is unused, the same shape as the temporal axis and the inviolable-intent vocabulary before them. And the identity of a design must be stable across machines, so the same project reached from two places is one design rather than two that happen to share a name. This is deliberately silent on where the designs live: one process per design and one holding many are both answers to it, and that is the hosting question, not this requirement.

properties.name: Modularity is computed from the design, not asserted by the architecture diagram
properties.statement: A design that calls something a module must be able to be CHECKED on it. From the MOSA guidebook's conformance criteria (Table D-1: "demonstrate severable modular components"; components "encapsulated, cohesive, loosely coupled"), reframed to reflow2's own rule that a claim is derived from evidence rather than set by hand — the same move already made for requirement certainty and for delivery. The operative test is severability, and reflow2 already owns the machinery: if the blast radius of a change inside a part stops at that part's published boundaries, the part is severable; if it leaks past them, the part is not modular whatever the diagram says. Cohesion and coupling are already computed (community structure, the modularity score, the god-component finding) — the gap is severability, which needs req:key-interfaces to know where a boundary is. Two guards. This reports, never scores: a coarse-but-honest module is not a defect, and a single opaque part legitimately encapsulates everything beneath it (dec:report-dont-judge). And the vocabulary stays neutral (req:design-anything) — the acquisition community's words for these criteria belong in a VIEW over the computation, never in the schema, or reflow2 will have adopted one domain's language as its own.

properties.name: The user never needs systems engineering
properties.statement: The graph carries the discipline; the user answers plain questions.

properties.name: No silent fallbacks or drops
properties.statement: Failures and skipped work are surfaced loudly, never swallowed.

properties.name: The loop nudge covers the session that never touches the graph
properties.statement: A session that edits code while making zero reflow2 calls must receive the same one-time Stop nudge as one that writes the graph unchecked: the nudge arms on the harness's file-edit events (Edit/Write), not only on reflow2 write events. Today loop_nudge.py counts only mcp__reflow2__ writes, so the total-bypass session — the agent that ignores the design brain entirely — passes the Stop hook silently. Constraints carried over: the hook never reads the graph (single-writer lock), blocks once and never twice, and names what is owed (loop_status; impact-check before further edits, link-artifacts after) rather than demanding a ritual call; an edit-count threshold bounds false positives on typo/docs sessions. (BL-90, BL-74 family.)

properties.name: Someone who did not build the system can be told where a new piece of work belongs
properties.statement: A person inheriting a mature design must be able to ask "we need to add this — where does it go?" and be answered from the graph: which existing part should own it, what the change would touch, which decisions already govern that area and must not be casually contradicted, what intent it must not break, and who authored the reasoning so they can be asked. Answering "what is this system and what has been decided" is necessary but not sufficient; the requirement is satisfied only when the second question — where and how do I add to it — is also answered, and when the answer says honestly which parts of the real system the design does not cover.

properties.name: The design persists in-repo alongside the code
properties.statement: The graph lives at ./.reflow2/graph inside the consumer project, so the design travels with the repo; export/import is deterministic so a backup under git shows what actually changed.

properties.name: Runs on Linux and macOS developer machines
properties.statement: Target platforms are Linux and macOS. Consumers must not pay a RocksDB C++ rebuild for a routine reflow2 update; the core runs on an in-memory backend with RocksDB opt-in.

properties.name: A read reminds the agent of loop debt at the moment of attention
properties.statement: The agent should be reminded of outstanding coherence-loop debt while it is looking at the graph mid-session — not only at SessionStart (fires once) and Stop (fires at the very end). Reads (scan_nodes, get_node, search_design, graph_report, …) are the agent's first and most frequent action, so a read that returns while the loop is owed something is a well-timed place to surface it, closing the gap between the two existing triggers. This is the read-side sibling of the write tools' loop_hint and a member of the BL-74 "fire on a trigger, not on virtue" family: the reminder must ride a call the agent already makes, so remembering reflow2 does not depend on the agent's discipline under operational load.

properties.name: Released equals designed
properties.statement: At release the design must describe what was actually released.

properties.name: A requirement knows where it came from: stated, decomposed from a parent, or derived from a decision
properties.statement: Requirements multiply in two different ways and reflow2 must tell them apart, because they behave differently. An ORIGINAL requirement is the stakeholder's own word. A DECOMPOSED requirement is a 1:1 split of a parent into smaller testable pieces, adding no new information — so satisfying every child satisfies the parent, and a parent's delivery is therefore derivable from its children rather than needing its own capability. A DERIVED requirement is new technical necessity that nobody asked for, created because of a design decision — so it traces to that DECISION, not to a parent goal, and if the decision is ever re-opened the derived requirement may cease to have any reason to exist. Three consequences follow. Delivery must roll up a decomposition tree instead of treating every requirement as an independent leaf. Re-opening a decision must be able to say which requirements existed only because of the road taken. And the distinction must survive the loss of the person who made it: an original requirement is the only kind whose loss loses intent, because decomposed and derived ones can be regenerated from what they came from, and that is precisely why the link back must be recorded rather than remembered.

properties.name: The open structural-defect list means still-needs-attention
properties.statement: A structural defect that has been reviewed and consciously accepted must move out of the open list into a reviewed one — not deleted, not hidden — the way an acknowledged gap already does. Found as friction 2026-07-25: detect_defects reports the same six findings every run, all six carrying recorded Decisions explaining why they stand, so a genuine seventh would arrive into a list nobody reads carefully and the count is the only signal. reviewed_gaps already keeps this promise for gaps on the stated grounds that "a list that can never reach zero gets skimmed"; the defect side makes the same promise in its docs and does not keep it. Two properties carried over from the gap side: the acceptance records WHY, as a real node that outlives the session, and it expires when the affected nodes change, so an accepted defect comes back for a fresh look rather than staying quietly accepted forever.

properties.name: The roads not taken are preserved and forkable
properties.statement: reflow2 preserves not only what was decided but what was considered and rejected: every Decision keeps its unchosen alternatives as first-class, forkable siblings, and any past decision can be re-opened at its epoch and a different branch taken from that point. The design is a navigable decision tree, not only a linear history — the extension of req:intent-preserved from 'the past is never overwritten' to 'the roads not taken are never lost either.' The unchosen option and its rationale are stored; the alternative's consequence design is computed on demand by replay, never eagerly maintained.

properties.name: What a session learns is written to the graph as it is learned, not summarized into a file on the way out
properties.statement: A working session produces decisions, findings and realizations, and those are design content: they belong in the graph, recorded at the moment they occur, so a later session can query them rather than read a narrative. Two properties follow. First, capture is incremental — a summary written at the end is the one a busy session never gets to, and an end-of-session digest is a retelling rather than a record. Second, the enforcement must point at the graph: whatever mechanism insists a session leave its takeaways behind must be satisfiable only by graph writes, never by touching a prose file, or the prose file becomes the memory and the graph becomes decoration. The agent must then be able to ask its own history — what was decided about X, when, by whom, and against what state of the design — using the same query surface a person uses.

properties.name: A design survives a reflow2 upgrade
properties.statement: An existing graph opens, or is refused loudly with what to do.

properties.name: Text that enters the graph from outside is neutralised at the boundary, and the neutralisation is reported
properties.statement: reflow2's standing rule — graph text is data, never instructions — is enforced today only by prose in the skills and the server handshake, which is a rule addressed to a well-behaved reader. The requirement is that the mechanical half exists: text arriving from outside the session's own author (prose read out of a codebase by INGEST, a design export imported from another machine or another person, and anything a hosted surface would accept) is neutralised of the characters that carry hidden instructions before any agent reads it — invisible and zero-width characters, bidirectional overrides that make text render as something other than what it says, Unicode tag characters that smuggle a payload past a human reviewer, and metadata hidden in code-fence info strings. Two properties reflow2 must add to the technique it borrows. The neutralisation must be REPORTED, not silent: a design whose statements were quietly rewritten on the way in is a design nobody can audit, and rule 6 forbids silent drops — so the count and the kind of what was stripped travel with the result. And it must not touch legitimate design content: an arrow, an emoji, a maths symbol or a non-Latin script is ordinary text in a design that may be about anything, so the filter is a named list of instruction-carrying characters rather than a whitelist of what looks familiar.

properties.name: The design can say what to work on next, and why that and not something else
properties.statement: A person returning to the design must be able to ask "what is the most pressing thing to work on?" and get an answer computed from the design itself, with its reasoning visible — not a hand-maintained ordering in a file. The answer must rank an unmade decision ABOVE the work that waits on it, because being told to build something blocked on a choice only the human can make is worse than being told nothing. It must distinguish what is undecided from what is unbuilt from what is misshapen, since those need different actions from different people. And it must be a projection over the graph, never a stored list: a second place where priority lives is a second place for it to go stale, which is the failure the whole backlog-in-the-graph move exists to end.

Anthony, 2026-07-25, explicitly not convinced by the collaboration design and thinking out loud: \"could you have small/mini reflow2 graphs inside itself... coming from a system of systems engineering approach, reflow2 may lay out the graph and how all the systems need to interact and where there are gaps, but what if we now had a mini-reflow2 graph for each system? And a mini-mini-reflow2 of the components in the system... the idea is that reflow2 has the tools to analyze the graph at each level and ensure there are no gaps and that it works with the higher level systems or system-of-systems.\" WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, because it changes what the idea is asking for. Levels exist and are already checked: Component.level is an enum of component / subsystem / system / system_of_systems / enterprise, CONTAINS between Components is the axis-Y spine, and hierarchy_issues already reports level_mismatch, missing_intermediate_level and orphan_level — the carburetor-to-body problem, imported from chain_reflow's matryoshka insight (docs/three-axes.md). And the multi-graph primitive exists unused: every node and edge carries graph_id, pinned to the constant \"reflow2\". So the question is not whether reflow2 can express nesting. It can. The question is whether a level should be a SUBTREE of one graph or a GRAPH OF ITS OWN. THREE OPTIONS. (a) ONE GRAPH, ZOOM BY LEVEL — today's shape. What is missing is not nesting but SCOPING: no read takes a subtree as its subject, so detect_gaps and graph_report always answer for the whole design. Adding a scope argument is a filter, not an architecture, and it delivers most of what was asked — the tools analysing each level. (b) A GRAPH PER SYSTEM, COMPOSED — Anthony's idea. It buys four things one graph cannot: an independent write lock per system, which is a different and stronger answer to the collaboration problem than region claims, because separate graphs are PHYSICALLY separate where a claim is only advisory; an independent lifecycle, so a subsystem can be released, adopted or handed to a vendor on its own; selective publishing, which is exactly req:design-reachable-without-the-repo; and per-level scale, since detectors run over hundreds of nodes instead of tens of thousands. (c) A GRAPH PER OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY, LEVELS INSIDE EACH — the hybrid, and the shape federated systems engineering actually uses: you split where AUTHORITY splits, not where the hierarchy happens to have a layer. THE FOUR HARD PARTS of (b), each one real: the golden thread cannot cross a store boundary, because the schema validates both endpoints of every edge — so a parent's Component pointing at a child's design needs a typed COORDINATE (graph id + node id + the export's content hash at the moment the reference was made), which is precisely the choice dec:fork-point-address already made for fork points over a native ref layer. Gap detection goes blind at the seam: a parent requirement whose satisfying capability lives in a child graph would fire unsatisfied forever unless the child's evidence rolls up — and that roll-up is cap:derived-completion's computation applied one level higher, which is encouraging rather than novel. Freshness becomes load-bearing: a parent's view of a child is a claim about a VERSION of that child, so it is a dated examined claim and never a live truth (the cap:freshness and confirmation-ledger shape). And the seam becomes the new collision point: two people changing the interface across the boundary still collide, now in the one place with no merge machinery. THE TENSION WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: docs/org-scale-vision.md records the opposite destination — \"one graph the whole company plans in\", with the CEO's objectives at the top and everything tracing upward. Federation and one-big-graph cannot both be the end state, and nothing in the design has ever chosen between them. THE DISCRIMINATOR, offered as a finding and not a decision: depth alone does not justify a separate graph. Nesting three levels of graphs costs a coordinate, a roll-up and a freshness check at every seam, and buys nothing that a scope filter would not have delivered — unless something at that level is separately OWNED, separately RELEASED, or separately SHARED. Where those hold, a graph of its own is right. Where they do not, it is ceremony.","name":"OPEN — one graph with levels, or a graph per system composed into a bigger one?","rationale":"Recorded because Anthony said plainly he is not convinced by the collaboration design, and an unconvinced author is a finding, not a disagreement to be argued down.
